newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, further losses seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 0.96 percent on Thursday, pushed down by a fall in ordinary shares of Dolenjska Bank, and traders said the downward trend was likely to continue as long as foreigners stayed away.
"The situation on the market is not rosy at all, and the current political climate does not indicate that foreigners would come back soon," said Andrej Ciuha, a trader at brokerage Inter Timex.

Traders said parliament's ratification of an association accord with the EU was likely to stimulate trade in the long run. The ratification was postponed on Wednesday to next week to allow political parties more time to reach an agreement on the issue.

The SBI index fell 12.64 points to close at 1,306.32, bringing its overall loss for the week to 4.08 percent. Turnover rose to 108.3 million tolars from 84 million. Overall, 11 shares fell, three rose, one was flat, and 13 were untraded.
"Don't ask me when the situation will improve. It will happen once foreigners return. Ask the central bank about that, it all depends on them," Ciuha said.
In February, the central bank put a damper on foreign buying, demanding international portfolio investors to open share trading custody accounts at one of 14 licensed Slovenian banks.
Since then, the SBI index has dropped by over 21 percent, while daily volumes have shrunk to a third of their previous levels.
Ordinary shares of Dolenjska bank were the most actively traded issue, falling 2.52 percent to 15,500 tolars on volume of 2,269 shares.
Traders said Dolenjska was down because of the share's poor liquidity, adding the stock could decline to about 15,000 tolars next week.
Mineral water producer and health resort operator Radenska led the day's decliners, tumbling 5.82 percent to 1,601 tolars on volume of 4,260 shares for total turnover of 6.9 million tolars.

"The decline is the result of a sell-off of small investors who bought shares in Radenska for privatisation vouchers and want to cash them in before the share falls further. But I think Radenska may have reached its bottom and should not fall any further," one trader said.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 7.14 percent to 7,500 tolars on volume of 50 shares.
Traders said the gain was due to technical reaction to Wednesday's 9.68 rise, but added that poor volume had made the jump less significant.
